## Description

Primary source:

<https://ngs101.com/single-cell-rna-seq-beginners-guide-part-5-cell-type-specific-differential-expression-proportion-testing-and-functional-pathway-analysis/>

Part 3 of 4. Pseudobulk differential expression: counts from all cells of a
given cell type in a given sample are summed, so that each sample (rather than
each cell) is one replicate. DESeq2 (negative binomial) is run per cell type and
limma-voom is used as an independent check.

Code is taken from the source article's code blocks. Changes made for this
notebook series: hard-coded values moved into the YAML front matter, paths built
from `params` rather than `setwd()`, and the fixes marked `FIX:` in comments.

## Load annotated Seurat object from tutorial 4

```{r step2_load_obj}
#-----------------------------------------------

annotated.file <- file.path(base.dir, params$annot.subdir, params$annotated.rds)
cat("Reading in annotated Seurat object:", annotated.file, "\n")
seurat_obj <- readRDS(annotated.file)

stopifnot(all(c(celltype.col, sample.col, condition.col, patient.col) %in% colnames(seurat_obj@meta.data)))
stopifnot(all(c(cond.ref, cond.test) %in% seurat_obj@meta.data[[condition.col]]))

DefaultAssay(seurat_obj) <- "RNA"
cell_types <- sort(unique(as.character(seurat_obj@meta.data[[celltype.col]])))
```

## Understanding the pseudobulk approach

Cells from the same sample are not independent replicates; the sample (donor)
is the biological replicate. Pseudobulk aggregation sums the counts of all cells
of one cell type within one sample, e.g. for CD14+ monocytes:

```
Before aggregation (cell-level):
  Healthy_1: 1,200 CD14+ monocytes (each with individual counts)
  ...
  Post_4: 950 CD14+ monocytes

After aggregation (pseudobulk):
  Healthy_1: Sum of 1,200 cells -> 1 pseudobulk sample
  ...
  Post_4: Sum of 950 cells -> 1 pseudobulk sample

Result: 4 vs 4 samples (proper biological replicates)
```

With only 4 vs 4 samples, power is limited, so few genes may reach significance;
that is an honest reflection of the replicate number rather than a failure of the
method.

## Create pseudobulk count matrices

```{r step3_pseudobulk}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 8: Create pseudobulk count matrices using PseudobulkExpression
#-----------------------------------------------

# Function to create pseudobulk for one cell type
create_pseudobulk_seurat5 <- function(celltype, seurat_obj) {
  # Subset to this cell type
  cells.ct <- colnames(seurat_obj)[seurat_obj@meta.data[[celltype.col]] == celltype]
  seurat_subset <- subset(seurat_obj, cells = cells.ct)

  # Use PseudobulkExpression to aggregate counts by sample
  pseudobulk_result <- PseudobulkExpression(
    seurat_subset,
    assays = "RNA",
    group.by = sample.col,       # Aggregate by sample
    layer = "counts",            # Use raw counts
    method = "aggregate"         # Sum counts
  )

  # Extract the RNA counts matrix
  pseudobulk_matrix <- pseudobulk_result$RNA

  # Convert column names back to match original sample_id format
  # (Seurat replaces "_" with "-" in aggregated group names)
  colnames(pseudobulk_matrix) <- gsub("-", "_", colnames(pseudobulk_matrix))

  # Return as regular matrix (required for DESeq2)
  return(as.matrix(pseudobulk_matrix))
}

# Create pseudobulk for all cell types
pseudobulk_list <- lapply(cell_types, function(ct) {
  cat("  Processing:", ct, "\n")
  create_pseudobulk_seurat5(ct, seurat_obj)
})

names(pseudobulk_list) <- cell_types

saveRDS(pseudobulk_list, file.path(diff.dir, "results/pseudobulk_counts_list.rds"))
```

## DESeq2 for each cell type

```{r step4_deseq2}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 9: Run DESeq2 pseudobulk analysis
#-----------------------------------------------

# Create sample metadata
sample_metadata <- unique(seurat_obj@meta.data[, c(sample.col, condition.col, patient.col)])

sample_metadata <- as.data.frame(sample_metadata)
rownames(sample_metadata) <- sample_metadata[[sample.col]]

# Make the reference level explicit so the contrast is test vs. reference
sample_metadata[[condition.col]] <- factor(sample_metadata[[condition.col]],
                                           levels = c(cond.ref, cond.test))

# Function to run DESeq2 for one cell type
run_deseq2_celltype <- function(celltype, pseudobulk_counts, sample_metadata) {

  # Get sample names from count matrix
  samples_in_counts <- colnames(pseudobulk_counts)

  # Verify that sample_metadata rownames match count matrix colnames
  if (!all(samples_in_counts %in% rownames(sample_metadata))) {
    stop("ERROR: Sample names in count matrix don't match sample_metadata rownames!")
  }

  # Order metadata to match count matrix columns
  sample_metadata_ordered <- sample_metadata[samples_in_counts, , drop = FALSE]

  # Create DESeq2 dataset
  dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
    countData = pseudobulk_counts,
    colData = sample_metadata_ordered,
    design = as.formula(paste("~", condition.col))
  )

  # Filter low-count genes (improve power and speed)
  keep <- rowSums(counts(dds) >= params$pb.min_count) >= params$pb.min_samples
  dds <- dds[keep, ]

  # Run DESeq2 analysis
  dds <- DESeq(dds, quiet = TRUE)

  # Extract results
  res <- results(
    dds,
    contrast = c(condition.col, cond.test, cond.ref),
    alpha = params$deseq.alpha
  )

  # Convert to data frame
  res_df <- as.data.frame(res)
  res_df$gene <- rownames(res_df)
  res_df$cell_type <- celltype

  # Add significance flag
  res_df$significant <- !is.na(res_df$padj) &
                        res_df$padj < params$de.padj &
                        abs(res_df$log2FoldChange) > params$de.lfc

  return(res_df)
}

# Run DESeq2 for all cell types
deseq2_list <- lapply(cell_types, function(ct) {
  run_deseq2_celltype(ct, pseudobulk_list[[ct]], sample_metadata)
})

names(deseq2_list) <- cell_types

# Combine results
deseq2_all <- do.call(rbind, deseq2_list)
rownames(deseq2_all) <- NULL

# Save results
write.csv(deseq2_all, file.path(diff.dir, "results/deseq2_pseudobulk_results.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Summary of significant genes per cell type
deseq2_summary <- deseq2_all %>%
  group_by(cell_type) %>%
  summarise(
    total_genes_tested = n(),
    sig_genes = sum(significant, na.rm = TRUE),
    sig_up = sum(significant & log2FoldChange > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    sig_down = sum(significant & log2FoldChange < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(as.data.frame(deseq2_summary), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Validation with limma-voom

limma-voom is an independent pseudobulk method; agreement between DESeq2 and
limma-voom increases confidence in a gene. Note the gene filter differs from the
DESeq2 one above (total counts rather than counts in a minimum number of
samples), as in the source article.

```{r step5_limma}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 10: limma-voom pseudobulk analysis
#-----------------------------------------------

# Function to run limma-voom for one cell type
# (named limma_paired_analysis in the article, but the design is unpaired:
# ~0 + condition, no patient term)
limma_voom_analysis <- function(
    counts,
    meta,
    design_formula = as.formula(paste("~ 0 +", condition.col)),
    contrast_str = paste(cond.test, "-", cond.ref),
    min_count = params$limma.min_count,
    voom_with_quality_weights = TRUE
) {

  # Order metadata to match count matrix columns
  meta <- meta[match(colnames(counts), meta[[sample.col]]), ]
  rownames(meta) <- meta[[sample.col]]

  # Convert factors
  meta[[condition.col]] <- factor(meta[[condition.col]], levels = c(cond.ref, cond.test))

  # Filter low expressed genes
  keep <- rowSums(counts) >= min_count
  counts <- counts[keep, ]

  # Create design matrix
  design <- model.matrix(design_formula, data = meta)
  colnames(design) <- gsub(condition.col, "", colnames(design))

  # Voom transformation with quality weights
  if (voom_with_quality_weights) {
    v <- voomWithQualityWeights(counts, design, plot = FALSE)
  } else {
    v <- voom(counts, design, plot = FALSE)
  }

  # Fit linear model
  fit <- lmFit(v, design)

  # Define contrast
  contrast.matrix <- makeContrasts(
    contrasts = contrast_str,
    levels = colnames(design)
  )

  # Fit contrasts
  fit2 <- contrasts.fit(fit, contrast.matrix)
  fit2 <- eBayes(fit2, trend = TRUE, robust = TRUE)

  # Get results
  res <- topTable(fit2, number = Inf, sort.by = "none", adjust.method = "BH")

  return(res)
}

# Run limma for all cell types
limma_list <- lapply(cell_types, function(ct) {
  cat("\nProcessing:", ct, "\n")
  limma_voom_analysis(pseudobulk_list[[ct]], sample_metadata)
})

names(limma_list) <- cell_types

# Process limma results
limma_all <- lapply(names(limma_list), function(ct) {
  res <- limma_list[[ct]]
  res$gene <- rownames(res)
  res$cell_type <- ct
  res$significant <- res$adj.P.Val < params$de.padj & abs(res$logFC) > params$de.lfc
  return(res)
}) %>% bind_rows()

# Save results
write.csv(limma_all, file.path(diff.dir, "results/limma_pseudobulk_results.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Summary of significant genes per cell type
limma_summary <- limma_all %>%
  group_by(cell_type) %>%
  summarise(
    total_genes_tested = n(),
    sig_genes = sum(significant, na.rm = TRUE),
    sig_up = sum(significant & logFC > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    sig_down = sum(significant & logFC < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(as.data.frame(limma_summary), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Compare methods (addition to the article)

The article recommends reporting genes that are supported by more than one
approach. This chunk tabulates, per cell type, the number of significant genes
for each method and the overlap. Cell-level results from part 2 are included if
that part has been run.

```{r step6_compare_methods}
sig_sets <- list(
  DESeq2 = deseq2_all %>% filter(significant) %>% transmute(cell_type, gene),
  limma = limma_all %>% filter(significant) %>% transmute(cell_type, gene)
)

findmarkers.file <- file.path(diff.dir, "results/findmarkers_celllevel_results.csv")
if (file.exists(findmarkers.file)) {
  fm <- read.csv(findmarkers.file)
  sig_sets$FindMarkers <- fm %>% filter(significant) %>% transmute(cell_type, gene)
}

key <- function(df) paste(df$cell_type, df$gene, sep = "|")

method_overlap <- data.frame(
  cell_type = cell_types,
  sapply(names(sig_sets), function(m) {
    sapply(cell_types, function(ct) sum(sig_sets[[m]]$cell_type == ct))
  }),
  DESeq2_and_limma = sapply(cell_types, function(ct) {
    length(intersect(key(sig_sets$DESeq2)[sig_sets$DESeq2$cell_type == ct],
                     key(sig_sets$limma)[sig_sets$limma$cell_type == ct]))
  }),
  row.names = NULL
)
print(method_overlap, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(method_overlap, file.path(diff.dir, "results/pseudobulk_method_overlap.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Genes significant in both pseudobulk methods
both <- intersect(key(sig_sets$DESeq2), key(sig_sets$limma))
write.csv(data.frame(do.call(rbind, strsplit(both, "|", fixed = TRUE))) %>%
            setNames(c("cell_type", "gene")),
          file.path(diff.dir, "results/pseudobulk_genes_both_methods.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```
